messages:
customer: acme-dev: Hey, hitting OAuth failures for both GitHub + Google logins in prod. Users see 'invalid_grant' or 'state_mismatch' right after redirect. Local & staging work. Any ideas?
Maya L: sorry you're blocked — can you paste the full redirect URL you configured in the app and an example failing callback URL we receive? also are you using a proxy/cdn in front of the callback?
customer: acme-dev: app redirect_uri set to https://app.acme.com/auth/callback (no trailing slash). Our callback logs show incoming request like: /auth/callback?code=Iv0...&state=eyJ... but the state in our server validation != the state param we issued.
Alex (support): common causes: 1) proxy/edge truncating or re-encoding query params, 2) browser appending a fragment (#) which isn't sent to server, 3) PKCE code_verifier mismatch (length or encoding), 4) double-URL-encoding of state. can you share server log snippet that compares issued vs received state (mask secrets)?
customer: acme-dev: here's a redacted log line from prod (timestamped):
```
[2026-02-12T14:12:03Z] oauth: verify state: expected=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5..., received=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiI%2FInR5... -> mismatch
```
Maya L: hmm received contains %2F (encoded '/'). Did something URL-encode state on the way? what's your client-side code that stores state before redirect?
customer: acme-dev: we use `sessionStorage.setItem('oauth_state', state)` and then do `window.location = authUrl`. On the server we compare `req.query.state` to session. Works in staging. Prod sits behind CF.
Ingrid H: I ran into this with another customer — CloudFront default behavior can normalize/encode slashes in query strings if you have certain caching policies or if a lambda@edge modifies the URL. Also some older proxies convert `+` to space when not marking as expected encoding, which breaks base64-state tokens.
SRE - Tom: can you dump the raw request line from the edge? e.g. in CloudFront logs or ALB access log (the raw query_string field). If the edge is altering it we should see the encoded form there.
customer: acme-dev: looking now, CF access log shows: `qstr=code=Iv0...&state=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiI%2FInR5...` so CF is encoding `/` as `%2F`. Staging doesn't go through CF.
Alex (support): aha. That explains it. Two remediation paths: 1) make state tolerant by URL-decoding before compare (but be careful re double-encoding attacks), 2) configure the CDN/edge to forward query strings without re-encoding. For GitHub/Google OAuth, best is to ensure canonical encoding at the edge.
Maya L: another immediate workaround — store a short opaque session id (e.g., oauth_session_id=UUID) in the state instead of a long base64 JWT. UUID survives re-encoding and avoids `+` `/` `=` issues. Then map it server-side to the full context. That is lower risk and cheap to roll out.
customer: acme-dev: thanks — we can patch client to use uuid state. Are there known issues with PKCE code_verifier encoding too?
Ingrid H: yes — code_verifier often contains `~`, `_`, `-`, `.` which are safe but some proxies choke on `+` or trailing `=` if it's base64url variants. The authorization code flow uses code_verifier->code_challenge; ensure you use base64url (RFC 7636) without padding.
customer: acme-dev: token exchange is failing sometimes with `invalid_grant` from Google. Log: `400: invalid_grant - code_verifier mismatch`. We compute code_challenge using `base64url(sha256(verifier))` and store verifier in session.
Alex (support): confirm that when the browser returns to /auth/callback you still have the same session (cookie flags, domain, SameSite)? If the session cookie isn't sent the server won't find the original code_verifier to validate. CloudFront cookie forwarding might be off.
customer: acme-dev: cookie domain is `.acme.com`, same site Lax, cookie present in requests according to CF logs. But we also recently added a redirect from http->https at the edge that rewrites the URL; maybe that's dropping cookies for the first hop.
SRE - Tom: try bypassing the redirect so the callback is handled directly by origin for a single test user. Also capture raw headers with curl to reproduce:
```
curl -v "https://app.acme.com/auth/callback?code=CODE123&state=STATE123" \
  -H "Cookie: session=SESSION_ID" \
  -H "X-Forwarded-Proto: https"
```
See whether session cookie ends up at origin.
customer: acme-dev: running that now — session appears at origin when we add the cookie manually. But real browser flows sometimes lose cookie on initial callback. We're using SameSite=Lax and auth redirect is a top-level navigation — should be fine normally.
Maya L: another edge case: mobile in-app browsers or some social sign-in flows open callback in a new webview without the original cookie jar. For those, using a server-side ephemeral binding (the uuid approach) helps too.
dev-portal-bot: Helpful doc: https://redwood.dev/docs/oauth-troubleshooting — see sections on PKCE encoding, CDN query string passthrough, and SameSite cookies.
customer: acme-dev: patch plan: 1) switch client state to short uuid, 2) add a defensive URL-decode step for incoming state compare, 3) audit CDN rules to stop re-encoding query strings. We'll test.
Alex (support): sounds good. after you deploy client change, ping here with a failing example if still broken. If you want we can do a joint repro session and SRE can tail origin logs.
Maya L: fyi for docs update — I'll add a short note about CloudFront encoding slashes and using opaque UUID state to the OAuth troubleshooting guide.
customer: acme-dev: thanks all, doing the rollout now. Appreciate the fast triage :thumbsup:
SRE - Tom: if the issue persists after the client-side change, we may add a temporary mapping middleware that canonicalizes state by decoding %2F/%20 and normalizing before compare to minimize customer impact while they roll out client fix.
